terms.definition: An object that lets old callback code resume a paused `async` function with a result.
terms.example: A continuation connects old callbacks to new async code.
terms.code:
let n = await withCheckedContinuation { c in
    c.resume(returning: 7)
}
print(n)

terms.definition: A function that turns a callback into an `async` call and checks that you resume only once.
A function that turns a failing callback into a throwing `async` call.
terms.example: Use withCheckedThrowingContinuation when the callback can fail.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Continuation, withCheckedContinuation and withCheckedThrowingContinuation in English?

dialogue.title: The old callback
dialogue.setting: An old API that still uses a callback

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I have an old function with a callback. How can I use it with await?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wrap it in withCheckedContinuation. It turns the callback into an async call.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is the continuation. A continuation lets the old code resume the paused async function.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Inside the callback, exactly once. withCheckedContinuation warns you if you forget or resume twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My old callback can fail with an error, though.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then use withCheckedThrowingContinuation. With that you can resume with an error.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. The error is thrown at the await line, so you can use try and catch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Great. A continuation connects old and new code.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. Do not store a continuation and forget it, because the function waits forever.
A continuation connects old callbacks to new async code.
